newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Labor Dept files suit against egg magnate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Labor Dept files suit against egg magnate.

text.p: The U.S. Labour Department, which has already hit the country's largest producer of brown eggs with a $3.6 million fine, said Friday it filed two lawsuits against egg magnate A.J. "Jack" Decoster to recover back wages.

One lawsuit alleges Decoster, owner of the privately-held DeCoster Egg Farm in Turner, Maine, "willfully and repeatedly violated" the federal fair labour standards Act by paying workers less than the minimum wage.
The second suit accuses Decoster of exploiting 82 migrant and seasonal farm workers by failing to pay them all they earned and not keeping accurate payroll records.
The suits did not specify how much money the Labour Department is seeking.

Decoster, in a written statement, said, "These filings relate to old cases, outstanding since the spring, as OSHA, knows full well...It is increasingly clear that OSHA is more interested in generating headlines than in fixing problems at the Decoster operation."

The Labour Department announced July 12 that it would seek $3.6 million in penalties for alleged violations of the Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA) by Decoster. At the same time, it announced it was seeking $45,000 in civil penalties for violations of the minimum wage laws.
Decoster is contesting both fines, said Labour Department spokesman John Chavez.

During a six-month investigation that ended in July, OSHA investigators found Decoster employees handling manure and dead chickens with their bare hands, and living amid rats and cockroaches in the company's trailer park. They found 12-to-17 workers kept in 10x60 foot trailers overflowing with sewage, officials said.

The facility itself was described as an "unsanitary, dangerous workplace. No means for workers to clean blood-soaked, diseased clothing. Exit doors locked, non-potable water," by U.S. Labour Secretary Robert Reich at a July press conference.
